authoringAndValidation.method: Read exact frozen source and prior repeat notes; inspect primary Punjabi commentary, compare short lexical/poetic alternatives and write new passage analysis, explanations and teaching questions. No modern translation was imported.
authoringAndValidation.bilingualStudyScope: English and Punjabi unit summaries with the established structured Study fields; no reader-schema change.
authoringAndValidation.sourceRecordAccounting: Counts remain 2/5/4/4/4/4/4. Chhand 61's paired clauses are all covered. Chhand 62's formula receives one explanation; the separate Chachari and Bhujang headings receive no invented line IDs.
authoringAndValidation.learnerLanguage: The teaching text uses line/ਤੁਕ; comparison flags, hashes and technical accounting are kept in the research file.
lookupLimits: No usable direct Mahan Kosh ਅਬਾਧ entry was recovered in the bounded lookup. The selected unhindered reading is attributed to Neki, and the Punjabi destruction-related reading is explicitly retained.
The underlying Bhai Vir Singh printed edition was not inspected. The two HTML pages are marked as derivative witnesses.
The downloaded Punjabi PDF was directly rendered and viewed; the Neki PDF was read as retrieved text, so those inspection methods are not conflated.
limitations: Assistant source research and another assistant's editorial review are not qualified Sikh/Punjabi review, approved translation or santhiya approval.
The frozen source's global 67-group caveat, local 62/67 comparison flags and all prior held sections, including Anand Pauri 24, remain unchanged.
The creation/conquest and unhindered/undestroyed alternatives are substantive interpretive choices rather than corrected scripture.
The explanatory safeguards concern the actual images in these lines: bodily inviolability, desire, fear, nurture, power, bliss, place, guise and lunar radiance.
